# Chapter One: The Kitchen

The kitchen always smelled of soy sauce and star anise. My grandmother Mei
cooked there every morning, and the enamel mug by the stove was hers alone.

She would call out "come and eat" and the house would fill.

We left in 1981, the summer my grandmother turned sixty-four.

Her sister Lin had married a man from Harbin, and they sent letters that took
three weeks to arrive.

"You were always the quiet one," she told me once, near the end.

I rode the red bicycle 2 miles to school, past 1200 houses just like ours.
